replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design confirms no password re-entry and 30-day cookie; concrete session-theft takeover via email change."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Ambient cookie plus immediate no-password update supports a distinct CSRF attack on the settings endpoint."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Immediate email change with no verification step is in design; spoofed recovery identity is a distinct flaw."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Immediate silent change of contact data supports lack-of-notice/repudiation harm distinct from takeover itself."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"30-day session cookie is explicitly in design; prolonged stolen-session access is a concrete attack."},{"id":"T6","keep":false,"reason":"Speculative: design never states a user-supplied account identifier; threat invents the parameter it attacks."},{"id":"T7","keep":false,"reason":"Repeats T5's attack (holding long-lived cookie) and harm (access to victim's stored PII).","duplicateOf":"T5"}]}
